item.title: Surviving Dementia Care: The Realities of Family Caregiving — Mon Sep 28, 6:30 PM — Gerrard/Ashdale
item.description: Are you a caregiver for someone with dementia? This talk addresses the specific experiences of people who are caring for a loved one, including the points of stress, the points of joy, and ways in which caregivers learn to survive the experience. Learn about understanding the diagnosis, communicating with the loved one, managing guilt and grief, choosing an assisted living facility, using music and the arts as a means of connection and how the loving bond within the family can be maintained for as long as possible. Presented by D. Grant Campbell, author of Surviving Dementia Care (University of Toronto Press, 2026). D. Grant Campbell is a Professor Emeritus of Library and Information Science in the Faculty of Information and Media Studies, at the University of Western Ontario in London, Ontario. Through a live demonstration, you'll see how custom skills transform modernization workflows by turning tribal knowledge into reusable guidance that scales across projects.
Join us to learn how to preserve organizational expertise while accelerating application modernization with AI.

item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Works by Daniel Schlick — Fri Oct 2, 12:00 AM — Northern District
item.description: Throughout the month of October, the works of artist Daniel Schlick are on display at Northern District library. Daniel Schlick is a multidisciplinary artist and photographer based in Toronto, Canada. Currently studying at OCAD University, his practice draws inspiration from travel, philosophy, and everyday experiences. Through photography and other media, Schlick explores the relationship between art, life, perception, and observation, guided by the idea that art reflects life while existing for its own purpose. "My photographic project follows confrontations with silence and searches for ruptures in the everyday world through which can be witnessed an unsettling sublimity. The monumentality of my works is equalled by the gravity of their presence, both tranquil and uncanny. I believe that photography's potency is its ability to investigate our intimacy with the world that surrounds us and to discover in it a very personal truth, the truth of what we desire from that very intimacy."
